title: fix(sse): stabilize SSE streaming chunking/framing for partial JSON & delimiter ordering
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming chunking and framing bugs that could emit partial/invalid JSON when delimiter tokens and event ordering were inconsistent. Improves stability for tool/function calling and OpenAI-compatible streaming clients.
description: Context: We observed intermittent client-side JSON parse errors in the SSE streaming path when using OpenAI-compatible adapters. Root cause: race between chunk boundary detection and partial JSON emission combined with delimiter token reordering during batching and flushes. Motivation: Fixes prevent partial JSON objects from being emitted, ensure stable event ordering (data, delimiter, done), and restore compatibility with existing SDKs and third-party streaming consumers. Summary of changes: 1) Introduces a deterministic chunk buffer state machine in runtime/sse that classifies tokens as json-payload, delimiter, or control and ensures atomized flushes when a JSON object boundary is complete. 2) Adds a delimiter-stability pass that reorders buffered delimiter events to always follow payload chunks. 3) Ensures the OpenAI-compat adapter (openai/compat/streaming_adapter.py and sdk-js src) maps internal events to SSE events in a stable order and avoids emitting an empty "data: [DONE]" before final payload. 4) Adds unit and integration tests reproducing the previous failure modes and a regression test that runs with simulated batching/flush races. 5) Minor docs updates describing the streaming guarantees and migration notes for custom consumers. Implementation notes: The runtime change is conservative; it keeps automatic batching/autoflush behavior but adds a short quiesce window (configurable, default 5ms) before flushes when a potential JSON token boundary is detected. This avoids splitting partial JSON without affecting steady-state latency significantly. Tests and validation: Added deterministic fuzz tests that simulate token arrival order permutations and a capture/replay test with real SDK clients. Benchmark: no measurable regressions for p50 latency; tail p99 improved slightly due to fewer client retries. Backwards compatibility: No protocol change; only emission ordering guarantees improved. Rollout: staged canary to dedicated clusters for 48h before global rollout. Merge and followups: merged via squash; follow-up work tracked in ENG-1399 to expose quiesce as a runtime tunable and ENG-1401 to add metrics for "partial_json_suppressed".

review_comments: Diego Morales (review): Great catch on the delimiter ordering. Two high-level asks: add a unit test for the quiesce timeout boundary and make the default 5ms configurable via env var.
Author reply (Ava Chen): Added unit test and made QUIESCE_WINDOW_MS configurable (runtime flag + env override).
Samir Patel (review): Minor: can we avoid a global lock in the fast path? The current implementation looks like it could contend under heavy batching.
Author reply (Ava Chen): Reworked the state machine to use per-stream atomic state and removed the global lock; added benchmark to show no regression.
